subject: Reducing memory usage in a matrix factorization model

messages.author: 6416ec9b5425a0d3
messages.subject: Reducing memory usage in a matrix factorization model
parts:
Hello,

I am working on what is essentially a matrix factorization model using
ADVI. I have two questions:

1) How do I reduce my memory usage? Fitting a model with 10,000 latent
factors uses ~19G on my machine. I would like to fit a model of
200,000 latent factors (runs out of memory), and eventually millions.

Where is the overhead coming from? According to my calculations, I
should only need 1.61 (GB 101 dimensions * 10000 factors * 8
bytes/double * 2 [one copy for means, one copy for standard
deviations] ] * 100 ELBO samples) to store 100 samples of the random
variables.

Could it be due to the overhead of constructing a large expression
tree for a for loop over all the observations? (See code below).

2) Is there a way to vectorize my two loops below?

The size of my dataset is

n_dim = 100 (dimension of latent variables)
n_words = 10000 (number of latent variables)
n_obs = 10,410,392 (number of observations)

It is only 269M in the RData format. Each observation is a scalar, and
the ratings matrix is represented in coordinate format (separate row
index, column index, and data vectors).

My model is the following:

data {
// Dimensions
int<lower=0> n_obs;
int<lower=0> n_words;
int<lower=0> n_dim;

// Hyperparmeters
real<lower=0> a_b;
real<lower=0> b_b;

vector<lower=0>[n_dim] a_w;
vector<lower=0>[n_dim] b_w;

// Data
int<lower=0> rows_[n_obs];
int<lower=0> cols_[n_obs];
real logx[n_obs];
}

parameters {
vector<lower=0>[n_words] inv_gb;
vector[n_words] b;

matrix<lower=0>[n_dim,n_words] inv_gw;
matrix[n_dim,n_words] w;

real<lower=0> sigma;
}

transformed parameters {
vector[n_dim] zero_vec;
zero_vec <- rep_vector(0, n_dim);
}

model {

inv_gb ~ inv_gamma(a_b, b_b);
b ~ normal(0, inv_gb);

for (v in 1:n_words) {
col(inv_gw, v) ~ inv_gamma(a_w, b_w);
col(w, v) ~ normal(zero_vec, col(inv_gw, v));
}

for (n in 1:n_obs) {
logx[n] ~ normal(dot_product(col(w, rows_[n]), col(w, cols_[n]))
+ b[rows_[n]] + b[cols_[n]],
sigma);
}

}

--
Sincerely,
Kui Tang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Reducing memory usage in a matrix factorization model
parts:
Yes, we have an arXiv paper now on the autodiff. Roughly, it's
about 40 bytes per expression evaluated in the log density.

What will help is if you vectorize these:

> for (v in 1:n_words) {
> col(inv_gw, v) ~ inv_gamma(a_w, b_w);
> col(w, v) ~ normal(zero_vec, col(inv_gw, v));
> }

Reduce this to:

to_vector(inv_gw) ~ inv_gamma(a_w, b_w);
to_vector(w) ~ normal(0, to_vector(inv_gw));

Note that the normal broadcasts, so you don't need a zero vector,
just the zero argument.


And this:

> for (n in 1:n_obs) {
> logx[n] ~ normal(dot_product(col(w, rows_[n]), col(w, cols_[n]))
> + b[rows_[n]] + b[cols_[n]],
> sigma);
> }

mu[n] <- dot_product(w[rows_[n]], w[cols_[n]]) + b[rows_[n]] + b[cols_[n]];

logx ~ normal(mu, sigma);
}

This is also moving w to a data type that's an array of vectors.
The reason to do this is both speed and size. It only has to do log(sigma)
once, and it cuts down the number of expressions from n to 1. And using
an array of vectors removes the need to copy out rows or columns.

- Bob
